extension_proof: For 0 <= d <= a=.491, T(d)=a-d and T(k*d)=a-k*d because 0<k<1. Thus q*T(0)+k*T(d)=q*a+k*(a-d)=a-k*d=T(k*d).
assumptions: Uniform baseline x on [-.509,.491], conviction iff final score > 0; boundary points have measure zero.
Target score deduction represents active deliberative reliance, not merely causal influence.
Model A complete excluder status independent of x; q fixed; exclusion occurs because of rule.
Model B every judge reduces target weight because of rule from .414 to .291, retaining positive weight.
Extension fixes q,k,baselines and manipulation-to-weight mapping.
Reported rounded rates idealized as exact population probabilities; actual counts are distinct.
conclusion: Formal claims preserved. Neither model estimates actual mechanisms or capacities; they differ in complete-removal achievement, not automatically in broader guidance.
